title: Abraham, When Severely Tried
description: Abraham, When Severely Tried in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: John Wesley printed these words in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 286. They first appeared in a book he and his brother Charles published together, and the Collection's own index cannot say which of the two wrote them.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Long Metre (8.8.8.8), and this page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: A-bra-ham, when se-vere-ly tried, His faith by his obe-di-ence showed, He with the harsh com-mand com-plied, And gave his I-saac back to God.

lines: Abraham, when severely tried,
His faith by his obedience showed,
He with the harsh command complied,
And gave his Isaac back to God.
His son the father offered np,
Son of his age, his only son,
Object of all his joy and hope,
And less beloved than God alone.
O for a faith like his, that we
The bright example may pursue!
May gladly give up all to thee,
To whom our more than all is due.
Now, Lord, to thee our all we leave,
Our willing soul thy call obeys;
Pleasure, and wealth, and fame we give,
Freedom, and life to win thy grace.
Is there a thing than life more dear?
A thing from which we cannot part?
We can; we now rejoice to tear
The idol from our bleeding heart.
Jesus, accept our sacrifice;
All things for thee we count but loss,
Lo! at thy word our Isaac dies,
Dies on the altar of thy cross.
For what to thee, O Lord, we give,
A hundred-fold we here obtain;
And soon with thee shall all receive,
And loss shall be eternal gain.

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788; John Wesley died in 1791.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788) or John Wesley (1703–1791), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
